anomalies.observed: On the MAIN PUMP & VALVE DRIVERS sheet, the gate of the main circulation-pump N-MOSFET T1 (IRLR2905, driven low-side via pre-driver T5/BT3904) is biased by R3 (10 kΩ) tied to +3V3, i.e. a pull-UP on the gate node NET0006. The structurally identical ATO-valve low-side switch T4 (AON6407, pre-driven by T7/BT3904) instead has its gate node NET0052 pulled DOWN to GND through R46 (10 kΩ).
anomalies.expected: For a low-side N-channel switch the gate must be pulled to GND so the load stays OFF when the driver is not actively sinking the gate (boot, MCU reset, T5/T7 off). The spec describes T2/IRLR2905 as a 'Main circulation-pump low-side switch' controlled as a GPIO on/off switch, and the matching ATO driver on the same sheet uses a GND pull-down (R46), confirming the intended topology.

evidence.quote: Main Pump: T5 BT3904 collector / T1 IRLR2905 gate node NET0006 connected to R3 10k whose top terminal is the +3V3 arrow (pull-up)
ATO Valve: T7 BT3904 collector / T4 AO3400A gate node NET0052 connected to R46 10k whose bottom terminal is a GND symbol (pull-down)
T2 — IRLR2905 (DPAK N-MOSFET) | Main circulation-pump low-side switch ... drives PUMP_MAIN net to the 24 V main pump load

anomalies.impact: With the gate pulled to +3V3 through R3, the main circulation pump is energised by default whenever T5 is not actively pulling the gate low (power-up, MCU reset, firmware not driving the pin, or a disabled GPIO). The board therefore runs the main pump continuously instead of switching it on command, contradicting the intended GPIO-controlled low-side switch and risking unintended circulation / overflow.
